rulings.decision: Append one entry to word_subs_before_codes in SP\1Cor\scholar_record\book_params.v1.json, after the existing 27. rulings.decision: Shape adopted with changes. File close/close_evidence.v1.json: {schema, book '1Cor', corpus_sha256, values}. values holds keys item_1, item_4, item_5, item_13, item_14, item_16, item_18, item_19, item_24, item_25 and OW-28, each {value, tier, source}. A value may be an object of named sub-values, each tiered the same way. tier is one of MEASURED, EXTRACTED, TRANSCRIBED, REPORTED, INFERRED, ASSUMED, UNAVAILABLE. source is {path, sha256, locator}. UNAVAILABLE is written as tier 'UNAVAILABLE' with value null, never as a value string. Contents and timing: before the reissue, item_1 (B-8 digits, l.26; retro part 'not due' under the R8-GATE-EVIDENCE construction); item_4 (E-23 digits; retro triage 'not due', same construction); item_5 (appeal state; retention enumerated with hashes); item_13 (capture-index verdict and the three layer counts separately); item_14 (capture-index --check verdict, _cure_verification.py verdict, census figures); OW-28 (spend in the notification unit against its ceiling, with the spend-unit measurement, gate l.610); item_24 and item_25 per R8-GATE-24-25. Then the orchestrator sets CLOSE_EVIDENCE_PIN to the file's digest and dry-runs. A lane's entry cites the file path, its sha256, the key, the value and the tier. It enters met true only on such a citation, and for items 16, 18 and 19 met false, type DUE_AT_CLOSE_ACT. Where a value the item needs is UNAVAILABLE, the lane enters met false with that item's own type, the tool refuses, and the orchestrator stops and reports to the owner (R8-GATE-EVIDENCE). Every source is a pinned file or receipt, never memory or a chat summary.
rulings.reason: The tool reads values['item_N'].value and .tier (l.394-395). The shape must say where UNAVAILABLE goes, so that it cannot be written where the tool does not look.
